sentences.text: The Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed challenging the award dated 21.05.2019 made in E.C.No.65 of 2016 on the file of the Commissioner of Workmen Compensation (Deputy Commissioner of Labour) Dindigul, served on 11.06.2019.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties herein are referred to, as per their rank before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts in a nutshell are as follows:
(i) The legal heirs of the deceased workman are the claimants before the Tribunal.
T h e f i r s t r e s p o n d e n t i s t h e o w n e r o f t h e v e h i c l e i n v o l v e d ,
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 14/05/2025 01:00:22 pm ) bearing Registration No. TN-49-H-4316.
The second respondent is the Insurance Company.
(ii) On 03.03.2016, the deceased Dharmaraj was working as a loadman on the first respondent's tractor bearing Registration No. TN-49-H-4316.

At about 05.00 p.m.
While loading sand from the riverbed at Santhana Varthini River near Moorthi thoppu, the said Tractor capsized.
As a result of which the sand fell on him and he was buried.
His body was recovered by the fire service only at around 11.00 p.m. on the same day, and he was declared dead.
(iii) The defence of the Insurance Company before the Tribunal is not that the accident occurred due to any violation of safety conditions that were required to be followed at the time of his work.

4. The learned Counsel appearing for the appellant / second respondent submitted that the Tribunal ought not to have proceeded to passed an order of compensation, as the deceased was allegedly engaged in the illegal activity in removing the sand from Santhana Varthini River.
Therefore, such activity cannot be considered as employment under the first respondent so as to attract the pursuance of Employees Compensation Act.

Section 2(1)(n)(i) and 2(1)(a)(c) of the Workmen Compensation Act, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 14/05/2025 The Branch Manager vs Ganthimathi on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72298921/
2 01:00:22 pm ) 1923, defines a workman as any person recruited as driver, helper, mechanic,
cleaner, or in any other capacity in connection with a motor vehicle.
However, this definition does not precisely explain the nature of the work to which a person may be engaged by the owner.
5. In view of the above, it is evident there is no dispute regarding the fact that the deceased was engaged as a loadman by the first respondent.
In terms of the definition under the Act, the Tribunal has rightly proceeded to pass an award of compensation in favour of the legal heirs of the deceased.
Accordingly, I do not find any merits in the order of the Tribunal.
Accordingly, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal stands dismissed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
